crime: {WITCH_NAME}'s father came home only some nights. One night he held her at the door for a long time, and he never came back. Since then, whenever anyone reaches to hold her, she steps backward through the nearest wall as if it were mist.

In the prison, a girl alone in her cell tells the corridor a chapter of a story each night after lockup, the way she used to for her little sisters at home. {WITCH_NAME} walks in through the bars and listens beneath the upper bunk.

One night the girl finishes the story. "The end. Now come here." She leans down from the upper bunk with her arms open. {WITCH_NAME} steps backward through the barred cell door, out of reach. Crying "Don't go," the girl reaches after her and falls headfirst from the bunk.

{WITCH_NAME} steps back in through the bars and kneels. A bleeding hand grips her cuff. As the girl whispers "Stay," {WITCH_NAME} pulls her cuff free and steps out through the bars. By morning the girl is dead.

In the trial court, the prisoners find the dead girl's blood on {WITCH_NAME}'s cuff. She says she left when the story ended. But the corridor heard "Don't go," then the fall, and only she could walk into a locked cell. The prisoners rule that she shoved the girl off the bunk.
She never touched the girl before the fall. The blood came from going back.
fields.epitaph: She walked away from every embrace, and was condemned for the one time she came back.
execution: The execution stand raises a high iron bunk bed with an iron girl on its upper tier. She stands chained upright below it. The iron girl leans down from the upper bunk with her arms open. The iron arms close around her chest, tighter and tighter. She hangs still in their hold, and the arms never let go.

magic.name: Mistwalk
magic.text: She slips through walls, doors, floors and objects like mist, as if nothing were there.
